first_in_archive: It's Been Nice Trippin' With Ya

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Particularly good, with the two drummers adding polyrhythms toward the end [13]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Described as especially cartoony, in a night of high energy and manic playing [6]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Cited as a classic version, along with Casey Jones and Hard To Handle [5]
- **Me And My Uncle** (1 other source): Unclear whether it came before or after Good Lovin'; uploader placed it after, following deadlists.com [2]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The late-set jamming, especially the jam in this song, stands out [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **It's Been Nice Trippin' With Ya**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **Six Days On The Road**: rare: 13 archived performances [16]
- **Glendale Train**: rare: 13 archived performances [16]
- **Dirty Business**: rare: 12 archived performances [16]
- **Lodi**: rare: 12 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-10-23.aud.wolfson.motb-0004.85071.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 27 songs; 137 min; rated 4.38/5 by 13 [1]
- **gd1970-10-23.aud-wolfson.sketchy-bontempo.12227.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 112 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd70-10-23.aud.wolfson.15080.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 15 songs; 91 min; rated 3.58/5 by 24 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording with audible bass and good balance, fairly good for an audience tape; Reviewer finds the audience recording poor, worse than many older recordings they have heard; Reviewer calls the recording fabulous and points to the taper's notes [4][7][9][10][11][12]

## Around the show

- Reviewer had a ticket but could not get into the show [5]
- Energy in the room was high, and the band sounded hot and jacked up [6]
- The crowd was fully with the band, who sounded very much on [9]
- Uploader first saw the Dead at Fillmore West in April 1970, after a cross-country VW microbus drive, on the Miles Davis opening run [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-10-23.aud.wolfson.motb-0004.85071.flac16**: taped by Cary Wolfson; transferred by D. McCabe; source: Audience by Cary Wolfson AUD > Sony TC-124 > MAC [1]
- **gd1970-10-23.aud-wolfson.sketchy-bontempo.12227.shnf**: taped by Cary Wolfson; transferred by sketchybontempo; source: Sony TC124 with a 1 point stereo mic 15 feet back from stage [2]. Also: Uploader gives a best guess at the lineage and source of this Wolfson audience tape [2]
- **gd70-10-23.aud.wolfson.15080.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Cary Wolfson; transferred by David Gans and Cary Wolfson; source: Audience [3]. Also: Credits Wolfson and Gans with recording and remastering the show [14]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead McDonough Arena - October 23, 1970](https://www.dead.net/show/october-23-1970) [17]
- Poster by Concertposterauction.com: [Grateful Dead Georgetown University Washington DC 1970 Concert Handbill + Review](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/428263/Grateful-Dead-Georgetown-University-Washington-DC-1970-Concert-Handbill-Review) [18]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1970-10-23 McDonough Arena, Georgetown U., Washington, DC - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1970-10-23-mcdonough-arena-georgetown-u-washington-dc/) [19]
- Poster by deadsources.blogspot.com: [October 23, 1970: McDonough Gym, Georgetown U, Washington DC](https://deadsources.blogspot.com/2019/02/october-23-1970-mcdonough-gym.html) [20]
